reason: 'Restored on normal boot' is not the whole story: the restore loop silently skips a stored record whose name the shipped manifest already declares, so a replacement under a shipped name only holds for the current boot.
evidence: core/niffler.nim:596-604 (`for item in ct.storeListItems("component")` … `if alreadyManifest: continue  # shipped manifest definition wins`, with no warning), :505-511 (the manifest's own binaries are started in the same boot), core/dispatch.nim:325-332 (`spawn` refuses an already-supervised name) and :347-357 (`kill` drops the children, so `kill` + `spawn` works for the current boot only).
old_string:
**Persistence of shape**: spawned components are recorded in the store
(kind `component`) and restored on normal boot.
new_string:
**Persistence of shape**: spawned components are recorded in the store
(kind `component`) and restored on normal boot. A stored record whose name is
also declared in `manifest.yaml` is skipped on restore — the shipped definition
wins, silently — so replacing a shipped component means editing the manifest; a
`kill` + `spawn` under the same name holds only for the current boot.
